subject.title: Model configuration accepts unvalidated model names, enabling silent misconfiguration

question: Should unknown configured model refs be warning-only in doctor/config validate, hard validation errors, or startup/runtime warnings, and which catalog source is authoritative for custom and forward-compatible providers?
rationale: The source can identify configured refs and catalog status, but warning versus hard-fail behavior affects existing custom providers, upgrade safety, and forward-compatible model names.

options.title: Warning-first validation
options.body: Add catalog-backed doctor/config warnings for unknown configured refs, with clear wording for untrusted or custom catalogs and no hard failure by default.

options.title: Strict validation
options.body: Reject unknown configured refs at config validation or write time, accepting a compatibility break unless an explicit escape contract is added.

options.title: Runtime-only handling
options.body: Keep config validation permissive and rely on startup warmup, runtime errors, and fallback notices rather than adding a new config/doctor analyzer.

recommendation.title: Warning-first validation
recommendation.body: Add catalog-backed doctor/config warnings for unknown configured refs, with clear wording for untrusted or custom catalogs and no hard failure by default.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest observed current-main history across config validation, configured model refs, and doctor checks, and the remaining blocker is a product/compatibility policy choice.
